newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares vault to new highs on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German shares vault to new highs on U.S. data.

text.p: German shares came to life to shoot to record highs in late trade on Friday, tracking a surge by Bunds and gains on Wall Street on the back of softer-than-expected U.S. economic data.

The IBIS DAX index spiked up to an all-time high of 3,504.27 points immediately after U.S. payroll data were released in the early afternoon, before easing to what was still a record close of 3,491.08, up 52.99 points.
Earlier the DAX index ended a lacklustre bourse session up 22.30 points, or 0.7 percent, at 3,460.37 points.
Activity was limited after Thursday's May Day holiday but dealers said liquidity should pick up next week and many expected fresh record highs.
The U.S. numbers showed a lower than expected rise in employment in April, which markets read as lessening the need for a U.S. rate rise soon.

Car shares remained in the spotlight as VW notched up an advance of nearly six percent to close late trade at 1,158.10 marks. Daimler-Benz rose 6.20 marks, or 4.8 percent, to 134.40 while BMW advanced 44.05 marks, or 3.1 percent, to 1,473.55.
No single factor appeared to be behind the interest in VW but dealers said the dollar's continued strength and technical buy signals were fuelling the gains.
"Car shares are simply in vogue at the moment," said a dealer.
The DAX-100 car share index, which tracks auto shares among Germany's top 100 listed companies, rose 3.1 percent, versus an advance of 0.6 percent for the DAX-100 as a whole.
Pharmaceutical group Schering AG, extending gains from Wednesday after it announced plans to buy back its own shares, rose 5.42 marks in IBIS trade to 170.47.
The resounding victory of Britain's Labour Party in the general election, ending 18 years of Conservative rule, had little impact on shares here.
Economists said that while Labour's approach towards Europe would be less hostile than that of the Conservatives, policy would not change much in the foreseeable future.
